No. The story does not have a balance between the two elements; instead, it relies almost entirely on 'scene'. 

Because the text is written in the format of a script or play, the entire narrative unfolds in real-time through dialogue and brief stage directions (actions). There is virtually no narrative summary or direct exposition to compress time or explicitly explain the characters' shared history and falling out. Instead, the reader must infer all background information (such as the three-year estrangement and the nature of their relationship) entirely from the subtext of their conversation and interactions.
